name: Acetylmorphone
summary: Acetylmorphone (dihydromorphinone acetate) is an opiate analogue that is an acetylated derivative of hydromorphone which was developed in the early 1900s as a potential cough suppressant and analgesic. It is prepared by the acetylation of hydromorphone using either acetyl chloride or acetic anhydride.

pharmacology.text: Acetylmorphone is not currently used in medicine, but may have a higher bioavailability than hydromorphone due to its greater lipid solubility, and hence is likely to be more potent than the parent drug, although probably slower acting due to the requirement for deacetylation to the active metabolite hydromorphone.

sideEffects.en: Little is known about it in people. Drugs of its class, the opioids, cause drowsiness, nausea, itching, constipation and pinpoint pupils. They can slow or stop breathing, and overdose can be fatal. Regular use leads to dependence and withdrawal.
sideEffects.zh: 目前對它在人體的作用所知甚少。與它同類的鴉片類藥物會引起嗜睡、噁心、皮膚癢、便秘與瞳孔縮小。它們可能使呼吸變慢甚至停止，過量可能致命。長期使用會導致成癮與戒斷反應。
sideEffects.zhHans: 目前对它在人体的作用所知甚少。与它同类的鸦片类药物会引起嗜睡、恶心、皮肤痒、便秘与瞳孔缩小。它们可能使呼吸变慢甚至停止，过量可能致命。长期使用会导致成瘾与戒断反应。

fact.en: It was made in the early 1900s, in the same wave of work on acetylated morphine derivatives that had produced heroin a few years earlier.
fact.zh: 它在1900年代初期被合成，屬於乙醯化嗎啡衍生物研究的同一波浪潮，而幾年前這股浪潮已產生了海洛因。
fact.zhHans: 它在1900年代初期被合成，属于乙酰化吗啡衍生物研究的同一波浪潮，而几年前这股浪潮已产生了海洛因。
